text:
Carolina arrives with its four-game winning streak snapped, a 4-1 loss at Nashville on Tuesday where Juuse Saros saved 2.6 goals more than the shots deserved. The Hurricanes are 4-1-0 in their last five and still without Jordan Staal, though Taylor Hall is day-to-day. The Islanders have had four days to stew on a 4-0 loss to Edmonton and are 2-2-1 over their last five, missing Matias Maccelli, Ryan Pulock and Calum Ritchie.

Our numbers favor Carolina, with 3.62 expected goals (the quality of chances) tonight to New York's 2.58. At five on five, the Hurricanes have taken 58% of the expected goals this season to the Islanders' 50%. Carolina's power play creates 0.98 expected goals a game against a penalty kill that allows 0.90, and New York takes 4.6 penalties a game. In net, the projected starters are Pyotr Kochetkov, +9.5 goals saved above expected (how many more shots he stopped than an average goalie would have) this season, and Semyon Varlamov, +5.7 in four starts, though Varlamov's .890 save percentage tells a different story. Ilya Sorokin has the other 10 starts.

Sebastian Aho is the Hurricanes forward to watch, at 36% to score and 73% for a point. Jackson Blake is on a seven-game point streak. For the Islanders, Bo Horvat is also at 36% to score and has taken Maccelli's spot beside Cizikas and Holmstrom. Matthew Schaefer, the first overall pick in 2025, gets a 63% shot at a point. Our under-the-radar pick is Carolina's Mark Jankowski, with 4.3 expected goals in his last 10 games, and a 42% chance of a point.
